title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 15-16
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 15 to 16 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'लोकाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षः कृताकृतः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 15 to 16 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 15 to 16.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 15 to 16** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **लोकाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षः कृताकृतः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**लोकाध्यक्षः सुराध्यक्षो धर्माध्यक्षः कृताकृतः । चतुरात्मा चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्दंष्ट्रश्चतुर्भुजः ॥** **भ्राजिष्णुर्भोजनं भोक्ता सहिष्णुर्जगदादिजः । अनघो विजयो जेता विश्वयोनिः पुनर्वसुः ॥**

He presides over the worlds, the gods and dharma. What is done and what is undone are all in his hands. The one of four forms and four arms is that God of gods. He shines in splendour, he is the food and the eater of it. The one who bears all, who was born before the world, is that God of gods. Sinless, the giver of victory, he comes again and again.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 15 to 16 mean?
faq.a: He presides over the worlds, the gods and dharma. What is done and what is undone are all in his hands. The one of four forms and four arms is that God of gods. He shines in splendour, he is the food and the eater of it. The one who bears all, who was born before the world, is that God of gods. Sinless, the giver of victory, he comes again and again.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
